documents.unit: University of Montana Teaching and Learning
documents.title: Teaching in the Age of Generative AI
tiers: Collaborative Exploration With GenAI Tools Encouraged
Use of GenAI Tools Encouraged with Attribution
GenAI Tools Allowed for Specific Tasks
Limited Use of GenAI Tools with Permission
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance asking every instructor to put a GenAI statement in the syllabus, with model statements from encouraged to discouraged, instructor-use disclosures, and talking points. It advises against AI detectors and sets out an educative procedure for suspected misuse.
documents.stance_why: The page makes no university-wide rule and instead tells every instructor to "include a brief statement" and supplies five model statements, from "Collaborative Exploration With GenAI Tools Encouraged" to "Use of GenAI Tools Discouraged"; it also gives instructor-use templates, a no-detector rule and a procedure for suspected misuse. The tiers make this delegates.

units.why: The page says how the guidance came about, "developed in response to those requests" from instructors; a statement about how the guidance was made is P84, general phase, informs.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this sentence ('The resources on this page were developed in response to those requests'). Source confirms it states why and how the guidance was produced (instructors asked for guidelines), a real if minor statement of origin; kept as P84, informs.
units.anchor: developed in response to those requests

units.why: Names the body that wrote the guidance ("faculty, staff, and administrators") and its scope across programs, so it describes how the policy was made (P84).
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A admin, B all). The sentence says faculty, staff and administrators wrote the guidelines; it addresses every reader and binds no one office, so all.
units.anchor: faculty, staff, and administrators have created concise, straightforward guidelines

units.why: Discloses that GenAI helped write the guidance itself, which is part of how the document was made (P84); no better type exists for this disclosure.
units.resolution_why: Type differs (A P48, B P84). The source says GenAI was used 'to summarize and refine language throughout this website', which is guidance text, not course materials (A's own fit_note says so). It tells how the guidance was made, so P84; B's fit_note keeps the disclosure aspect. Actor all. Other coder notes kept: A fit_note (for their type): This is disclosure of AI use in making the guidance page itself, not course materials as such.
units.anchor: GenAI was used to summarize and refine language
units.fit_note: Also a disclosure of AI use in producing the guidance, not only a description of the drafting process.

units.why: The guidance is declared provisional ("will continue to change"), which is P54, a revisit-regularly statement.
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A admin, B all). Statement that the information 'will continue to change' addresses all readers; all.
units.anchor: will continue to change as the needs of our campus change

units.why: 'we hope that you will be an active voice in those conversations' invites readers to join continuing campus conversations on the guidance. That is P54 (feedback invited), addressed to all readers, and 'hope' makes it a should.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. Source: 'we hope that you will be an active voice in those conversations' sits beside the sentence that the guidance will change; it invites feedback, which P54 covers. Kept. A had actor instructor; the invitation addresses all readers, so all.
units.anchor: we hope that you will be an active voice in those conversations

units.why: Points faculty to the Library's 'regularly-updated guide to Artificial Intelligence' for introductory information, citing and copyright; this supports instructors in learning about AI (P63).
units.resolution_why: Type and actor differ (A P63 instructor before-course should; B P72 all general should). The sentence points readers to the Mansfield Library's AI guide for keywords, ethics, citing AI and copyright. On this faculty-facing page the readers are mainly instructors learning about GenAI, so P63; P72 is for pointing students to human help, and a web guide is not that. Both coders' fit_notes record the guide is a resource, not a person. Other coder notes kept: B fit_note (for their type): Points to a library guide (a resource) rather than to a person or service.
units.anchor: we encourage you to explore the Mansfield Library
units.fit_note: Resource pointer for keywords, disinformation, ethics, citing AI and copyright, not a workshop or consultation.

units.why: "All instructors should include a brief statement" is a recommendation that every syllabus carry an AI statement, which is P09; modality should because of the word 'should'.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B course-start). The sentence tells instructors to put a statement in the syllabus, which communicates expectations; course-start, as for other P09 units.
units.anchor: All instructors should include a brief statement in their course syllabus

units.why: 'Whether you welcome, limit, or discourage their use' leaves the stance to each instructor, so the university sets no default (P04).
units.anchor: Whether you welcome, limit, or discourage their use, having clear expectations benefits everyone

units.why: Gives a reason for the syllabus statement: it "promotes academic integrity" by marking boundaries. Fits P95 (honesty as the reason) better than P09, which is the duty to include a statement.
units.resolution_why: Type differs (A P09, B P95). 'A clear GenAI statement helps students understand the boundaries between acceptable assistance and academic dishonesty' gives integrity as the reason for the syllabus statement, so P95 (reason grounded in academic honesty); the duty itself is the separate P09 unit. Both coders' fit_notes agree the reason is integrity. Other coder notes kept: A fit_note (for their type): Gives academic integrity as the reason for a syllabus statement.
units.anchor: boundaries between acceptable assistance and academic dishonesty
units.fit_note: The reason is clarity about boundaries, not fairness to other students.

units.why: The page lists reducing student anxiety as a reason for the statement and says guidance "builds trust"; a reason for communicating expectations (P09), informs.
units.anchor: provides clarity and builds trust
units.fit_note: Reason given: student anxiety and trust, 'whether restrictive or permissive'. States a benefit (less anxiety, more trust) of having a statement, not the duty itself.

units.why: 'Support equity' argues that transparent expectations give more equitable access through familiarity; equity of access is P51, though it is not a rule about cost.
units.anchor: also supports more equitable GenAI access through increased student familiarity
units.fit_note: Equity here means familiarity with tools, not cost or alternatives. Equity through familiarity and transparency, not through free access or alternatives.

units.why: Says a policy can open discussion of how students can "engage with it meaningfully"; recommends talking about AI with students (P66).
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'A well-crafted policy can open the door to discussing not just if students can use AI, but how they can engage with it meaningfully'. It tells instructors a policy is a basis for discussing AI with students, a real statement, P66.
units.anchor: can open the door to discussing not just

units.why: A benefit claim ("support learning, creativity, and critical reflection") with no rule: P87.
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A instructor, B all). 'GenAI can support learning, creativity, and critical reflection' is a general claim about benefits for everyone, so all.
units.anchor: GenAI can support learning, creativity, and critical reflection

units.why: Frames the syllabus statement as aligned with institutional goals ("academic excellence and innovation"); an institution-wide framing statement, P56.
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A instructor, B all). 'As a university, we aim to foster both academic excellence and innovation' is an institutional framework statement for all readers, so all. Topics merged.
units.anchor: we aim to foster both academic excellence and innovation
units.fit_note: Institutional goals offered as reason for the syllabus statement.

units.why: Says stronger statements should be 'tailored to the academic values of your discipline and pedagogy', so rules follow the course's aims (P83).
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. Source: 'Stronger statements will also include language tailored to the academic values of your discipline and pedagogy'. It is advice on how to word the syllabus statement, a real instruction, P83 (fit is partial, noted).
units.anchor: Stronger statements will also include language tailored to the academic values of your discipline
units.fit_note: Ties the statement to the academic values of the discipline and pedagogy, not to course learning outcomes.

units.why: 'in a coding class, collaboration with tools might be part of the process' is an example, in the same sentence as the discipline-tailoring advice, of what a statement might say. It is an illustration, not a rule, so it is coded informs under P83 (align with the discipline), not as a default stance.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this (as P02, should/may, permit). Source: 'in a coding class, collaboration with tools might be part of the process' is an illustration of discipline-tailored wording. It sets no default and uses 'might', so P02 overstates it; recoded P83, informs, neutral. Kept because it names coding classes, the project's focus. Other coder notes kept: A fit_note (for their type): Only a suggestion for what a statement might say in a coding class.
units.anchor: in a coding class, collaboration with tools might be part of the process

units.why: The instructor is the one who crafts the policy, P04 (instructors set the rule), informs.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'Creating a policy requires deep consideration by the instructor' says the policy is the instructor's to create, P04, informs. Kept.
units.anchor: Creating a policy requires deep consideration by the instructor

units.why: 'very difficult to track and identify because it is being built in to systems students already use' admits AI cannot be fully verified, so P82. It also names embedded AI (Adobe, Copilot) but sets no rule, so not P07.
units.anchor: the nature of gen AI makes it very difficult to track and identify
units.fit_note: Also notes AI embedded in Adobe PDF reader, library databases and Microsoft Copilot, which students may be required to use. Also names embedded AI in Adobe PDF reader, library databases and Copilot (P07 content), but states no rule about it.

units.why: The 'Collaborative Exploration' template says students 'will be encouraged to use generative AI tools to draft, brainstorm, research, revise, and reflect', an encouraging default, so P02.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A during-work, B course-start). The sample statement tells students how to use AI in the work, so during-work (rules that bind the work). Modality should kept: 'You will be encouraged to use'.
units.anchor: encouraged to use generative AI tools to draft, brainstorm, research, revise, and reflect

units.why: Same template makes use conditional on transparency; disclosure of AI use (P24).
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'but always with transparency' is the condition on the encouraged use in the same sample statement, a disclosure expectation (P24). Kept; B's fit_note records that how to be transparent is not said. unit_stance permit (condition on allowed use).
units.anchor: but always with transparency
units.fit_note: Template wording says 'transparency' without saying how.

units.why: The template promises class discussion and teaching of ethical use for academic and professional contexts: P44 (teach effective AI use as professional skill).
units.resolution_why: Phase and actor differ (A student during-work, B instructor course-start). The sample statement says 'We will discuss how to use these tools critically and ethically', a commitment by the instructor, so actor instructor; the discussion happens in the course, so during-work. Type P44 agreed.
units.anchor: We will discuss how to use these tools critically and ethically
units.fit_note: Emphasizes critical and ethical use as well as professional use.

units.why: The 'Encouraged with Attribution' template says AI tools 'are welcome in this course as aids to your learning', so permit or encourage by default (P02).
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A during-work, B course-start). The statement tells students AI tools are welcome in their work, so during-work.
units.anchor: are welcome in this course as aids to your learning, provided you use them responsibly

units.why: Students must acknowledge or cite "substantial AI contributions" such as text, code or analysis, which is P24 with a threshold of 'substantial'.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance differs (A require, B permit). The statement asks students to acknowledge or cite substantial AI contributions. It requires disclosure, not AI use, and the use itself is welcome with attribution, so permit.
units.anchor: asked to acknowledge or cite any substantial AI contributions
units.fit_note: Disclosure is required only for 'substantial' contributions. Applies only to substantial contributions, not all AI use.

units.why: The 'Allowed for Specific Tasks' template lists 'summarizing texts, finding sources, generating initial coding ideas'; the nearest type is brainstorming and exploring approaches (P15), as no type covers permission for a named task list.
units.anchor: You may use generative AI tools for specific tasks in this course
units.fit_note: A narrow list of permitted tasks (summarizing, finding sources, initial coding ideas); not only brainstorming. Task list also includes summarizing texts and finding sources, and is a narrow permission, not just brainstorming.

units.why: Requires documenting "what tools you used and how"; this names the tool and how it was used, closer to P25 than P24.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance differs (A require, B permit). 'you must clearly document what tools you used and how' requires documentation of an allowed use; the use is permitted, so permit.
units.anchor: you must clearly document what tools you used and how
units.fit_note: Asks for tools and manner of use, not the exact prompt or output.

units.why: Student must verify AI output, "responsible for verifying the accuracy"; P31.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance differs (A require, B permit). 'You are responsible for verifying the accuracy of any AI-generated content' is a duty attached to allowed use, so permit.
units.anchor: responsible for verifying the accuracy of any AI-generated content

units.why: The 'Limited Use with Permission' template: use 'is permitted only with prior instructor approval', so the instructor decides case by case (P04); the unit stance is restrict because the default is no use without approval.
units.anchor: is permitted only with prior instructor approval
units.fit_note: Also fits P06, a fallback when permission is absent; chosen P04 because approval is case by case. Approval is requested per use, but the default is no AI.

units.why: Student must consult the instructor before using AI; asking first is P10.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'If you wish to use these tools to brainstorm ideas, locate sources, generate content, or get feedback, please consult with me first' is a separate sentence from the approval rule and tells students to ask first. P10 fits partly (it is a requirement for all use, not only when unsure), so fit_note added.
units.anchor: please consult with me first
units.fit_note: Asking is required before any use in this tier, not only when a student is unsure.

units.why: The same template: 'Unauthorized use may be considered a violation of academic honesty', treating unauthorized AI as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Unauthorized use may be considered a violation of academic honesty

units.why: The 'Discouraged' template says AI 'is discouraged for any assignment or activity', which P03 covers; its other sentences carry the actual rules, coded separately.
units.anchor: is discouraged for any assignment or activity in this course
units.fit_note: Labelled discouraged, but the next sentences make use a violation, so the template acts as a ban. The following sentence in the same template makes use a violation, so it is more than discouragement.

units.why: Students must submit their own original work, P29.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance differs (A require, B restrict). 'All submitted work must be your own original effort' sits in the discouraged tier and limits AI help; it does not require AI use, so restrict.
units.anchor: All submitted work must be your own original effort

units.why: 'Use of these tools will be treated as a violation of academic integrity policies' classifies use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Use of these tools will be treated as a violation of academic integrity policies

units.why: Recommends instructors state their own AI use to students, with the reason: transparency and modeling. This is P47, informs.
units.resolution_why: Modality differs (A should, B informs). 'Using instructor statements creates transparency by openly communicating how, when, and why AI tools are used' states what instructor statements do; it gives no instruction, so informs.
units.anchor: Using instructor statements creates transparency

units.why: Template for an instructor who discloses no AI use in the course: P47.
units.resolution_why: Modality differs (A may, B informs). 'I have not used generative AI tools in the preparation, design, or delivery' is a sample disclosure of the instructor's own non-use; it reports a fact, so informs.
units.anchor: I have not used generative AI tools in the preparation, design, or delivery

units.why: Template commits that AI will not assess student work, apart from Canvas-embedded tools. A human-grades commitment (P46) and also a limit disclosed to students (P47); I choose P46 because of "assess any of your work".
units.resolution_why: Type, phase, modality and unit_stance differ (A P47 course-start may neutral; B P46 during-assessment must-not restrict). 'Your instructor will not use AI tools to assess any of your work' is a commitment that AI will not assess work, which P46 (humans, not AI, assess) names directly; P47 only covers disclosure. It governs assessment, so during-assessment, and 'will not' is a commitment, so must-not. A's fit_note (Canvas-embedded tools are excepted) is kept as a fit note on B's unit. Other coder notes kept: A fit_note (for their type): Exception: tools embedded in Canvas to organize the course.
units.anchor: will not use AI tools to assess any of your work
units.fit_note: Also an instructor disclosure to students and carves out Canvas-embedded tools.

units.why: Template statement that no course materials were AI-generated, an instructor disclosure about materials: P48 covers materials; P47 is disclosure of the instructor's own use. Chose P47 because this states no use.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'None of the content, resources, or assignment guidelines in this course were generated using AI' is a second statement in the same template, a disclosure that materials were not AI-made. Kept as P47, informs.
units.anchor: None of the content, resources, or assignment guidelines in this course were generated using AI

units.why: Template that discloses AI help in assignment design: P47.
units.resolution_why: Modality differs (A may, B informs). 'I have used AI tools to help brainstorm or refine assignment prompts' reports the instructor's use, so informs.
units.anchor: used AI tools to help brainstorm or refine assignment prompts

units.why: Template for disclosing AI-made materials, P48.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'Some instructional materials ... have been created or enhanced using generative AI tools' is the disclosure sentence before the review sentence A coded. Kept, P48, informs.
units.anchor: have been created or enhanced using generative AI tools

units.why: 'All AI-generated content has been reviewed and edited to ensure accuracy and alignment with course goals' is part of the sample statement disclosing AI-made materials (P48). It reports what the instructor did, so informs, given to students at course-start.
units.resolution_why: Modality differs (A may, B informs) and phase (B before-course). 'All AI-generated content has been reviewed and edited to ensure accuracy' reports what the instructor did, in a statement given to students, so informs at course-start.
units.anchor: All AI-generated content has been reviewed and edited to ensure accuracy

units.why: Template disclosing AI drafting of announcements; instructor use for teaching work, disclosed: P47.
units.resolution_why: Type, modality and unit_stance differ (A P59 may permit; B P47 informs neutral). The statement 'I occasionally use AI tools to draft routine communications' is a sample disclosure to students, which P47 covers; the review commitment in the next sentence is coded separately as P59. A's fit_note is kept in this note: it adds that messages are 'always reviewed before being sent'. Other coder notes kept: A fit_note (for their type): Adds that messages are 'always reviewed before being sent'.
units.anchor: I occasionally use AI tools to draft routine communications

units.why: Instructor reviews AI-drafted messages before sending; human review of AI output, P59.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'These messages are always reviewed before being sent' is a human-review condition on AI-drafted communications, P59, informs. Kept.
units.anchor: always reviewed before being sent
units.fit_note: A review commitment about AI-drafted communications.

units.why: Template disclosing AI-made feedback examples: P47.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'Some examples of feedback or model responses ... may have been generated with the help of AI tools' is the disclosure sentence of the feedback-examples template. Kept, P47, informs.
units.anchor: feedback or model responses provided in this course may have been generated

units.why: 'I verify and adapt all examples to reflect course standards and expectations' is the instructor's own disclosure in the feedback-examples template (P47). It states a practice rather than instructing anyone, so informs.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. Source: 'I verify and adapt all examples to reflect course standards and expectations' is the second sentence of the feedback-examples template, a separate claim about instructor verification. Kept as P47; A's modality may changed to informs because it reports a practice.
units.anchor: I verify and adapt all examples to reflect course standards and expectations
units.fit_note: Also states AI-drafted feedback examples are verified by the instructor.

units.why: 'When I use AI tools in course preparation or delivery, I will let you know' commits the instructor to disclose their AI use to students. It is P47. 'I will let you know' is a commitment, so must.
units.resolution_why: Modality differs (A should, B informs). 'I will let you know' is a first-person commitment to disclose in the sample statement, an obligation the instructor takes on, so must. Type P47 agreed.
units.anchor: When I use AI tools in course preparation or delivery, I will let you know

units.why: 'You are encouraged to ask questions about how AI fits into our classroom practice' invites students to discuss the instructor's AI use in class. That is explaining and discussing AI practice with students (P66), addressed to students as a should.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this (as P10). Source: 'You are encouraged to ask questions about how AI fits into our classroom practice' invites questions about the instructor's own AI use, not about whether a student's use is allowed (B's own fit_note says so). Recoded P66 (discuss AI with students). B's fit_note moved here. Other coder notes kept: B fit_note (for their type): Invites questions about the instructor's AI use generally, not only about whether a use is allowed.
units.anchor: encouraged to ask questions about how AI fits into our classroom practice

units.why: Offers talking points so instructors introduce the policy in class; P66 (explain and discuss the rules).
units.resolution_why: Modality differs (A should, B may). 'a simple outline of topics you might use for a short comment' is optional, so may.
units.anchor: a short comment when introducing your syllabus or gen AI policy

units.why: The script says 'you might have a different gen AI policy in each of your classes', i.e. each course's policy is separate (P11).
units.anchor: you might have a different gen AI policy in each of your classes

units.why: 'Generative AI can be helpful, but it can also be misleading, biased, or inaccurate' warns that output can be wrong, which P31 covers.
units.anchor: it can also be misleading, biased, or inaccurate

units.why: The script mentions 'the environmental impacts of Gen AI' as a matter to discuss, so P53.
units.anchor: about the environmental impacts of Gen AI

units.why: Script tells students the syllabus carries the AI rules; students check the syllabus. P78 fits (students follow each course's rules) but modality is informs; chosen over P09, which binds instructors.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'You'll see a short statement in the syllabus about how I expect you to use—or not use—AI in this class' is a talking point that points students to the syllabus. Kept as B coded it, P78, informs; B's fit_note records that it is framed as the instructor's action.
units.anchor: a short statement in the syllabus about how I expect you to use
units.fit_note: Stated as what the instructor will do, not as a student duty.

units.why: Direct instruction to ask the instructor when unsure: P10.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A course-start, B during-work). 'If you're ever not sure what's allowed, just ask me' applies when a student is working and unsure, so during-work (the usual phase for P10).
units.anchor: If you’re ever not sure what’s allowed, just ask me

units.why: 'faculty should not use AI detection tools because UM does not have an enterprise contract' forbids faculty detector use, so P39 (not P40, which approves detectors).
units.anchor: faculty should not use AI detection tools because UM does not have an enterprise contract

units.why: 'the university cannot guarantee the privacy or security of student work' is a data privacy reason for the detector ban, so P50.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. Source: 'the university cannot guarantee the privacy or security of student work' is a separate reason, given before the sentence on intellectual property. Kept as P50, informs.
units.anchor: the university cannot guarantee the privacy or security of student work

units.why: 'uploading assignments to third-party tools constitutes an unfair and unapproved use of students' intellectual property' tells faculty not to upload student work to outside tools, and the stated ground is students' intellectual property. P52 (ownership of inputs) names that ground; the privacy reason is a separate unit under P50. The sentence is strong, so must-not.
units.resolution_why: Type and modality differ (A P52 should-not; B P50 must-not). The source states the ground as 'students' intellectual property' and the privacy reason is a separate sentence part coded in its own unit, so P52. 'constitutes an unfair and unapproved use' is stated as a prohibition, so must-not rather than should-not.
units.anchor: uploading assignments to third-party tools constitutes an unfair and unapproved use

units.why: 'unreliable and should not be used as sole evidence of misconduct' limits detector output to supporting evidence, which P69 covers (broadened).
units.anchor: should not be used as sole evidence of misconduct

units.why: Explains detectors are unreliable and biased against multilingual and neurodivergent writers, supporting not relying on them: P39, informs.
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A instructor, B all). 'AI detectors frequently produce false positives' is a fact about detectors for all readers, so all.
units.anchor: AI detectors frequently produce
units.fit_note: Names multilingual writers, neurodivergent students and non-standard writing styles as at risk of false flags.

units.why: "Not admissible proof" sets an evidence standard for misuse findings: P69, chosen over P39 as it says what counts as proof.
units.resolution_why: Type and unit_stance differ (A P39 restrict; B P69 neutral). 'Detection results are not admissible proof of academic dishonesty' sets an evidence standard, as the preceding 'sole evidence' unit does (both coders chose P69 there), so P69. It restricts detector use as proof, so restrict, as for that preceding unit.
units.anchor: Detection results are not admissible proof

units.why: 'Conversations and context matter more than software scores' sets what evidence to weigh, P69.
units.resolution_why: Type differs (A P69, B P57). 'Conversations and context matter more than software scores' weighs kinds of evidence (conversation and context over detector scores), which is P69; the talk-first step is a separate unit (P57).
units.anchor: Conversations and context matter

units.why: 'Fair and educational responses should focus on transparency, student intent, and clarity of course policy' is an educative response to misuse (P68).
units.anchor: Fair and educational responses

units.why: 'Treating AI misuse as a moment for learning, not just discipline' sets an educative response, so P68.
units.anchor: Treating AI misuse as a moment for learning, not just discipline

units.why: 'Instructors are encouraged to connect with their colleagues and/or seek conversation and support' from the Associate Director, support for faculty (P63).
units.anchor: Instructors are encouraged to connect with their colleagues
units.fit_note: Support is for handling suspected misuse, not for learning AI.

units.why: Step 1 tells instructors to 'Review your syllabus policy to confirm how clearly it was stated' before acting; gathering context before escalating is P57.
units.resolution_why: Type differs (A P57, B UNCOVERED). 'Review your syllabus policy to confirm how clearly it was stated' is a step before taking action on suspected misuse, a way of gathering context before escalating, so P57 fits partly (noted). B's uncovered_note: 'Before acting on suspected misuse, the instructor checks how clear their own syllabus AI policy was.' Other coder notes kept: B uncovered_note (for their type): Before acting on suspected misuse, the instructor checks how clear their own syllabus AI policy was.
units.anchor: Review your syllabus policy to confirm how clearly it was stated
units.fit_note: The context to gather first is the clarity of the instructor's own syllabus policy, not facts about the student.

units.why: 'Suspicion alone is not proof' sets an evidence standard (P69).
units.anchor: Suspicion alone is not proof

units.why: 'Schedule a private, non-confrontational meeting with the student' is talking with the student first (P57).
units.anchor: Schedule a private, non-confrontational meeting with the student

units.why: In the meeting the instructor invites the student to explain their process, which also lets the student respond: P64 (right to respond) fits less well than P57, which is the talk-first step.
units.resolution_why: Type differs (A P64, B P57). 'Invite the student to describe their process in detail' is part of the low-stakes conversation to gather context before any escalation (P57). It does not set out a right to respond to allegations (P64); A's fit_note says it is 'framed as a conversation to understand process'. B's fit_note kept: it also gives the student a chance to respond. Other coder notes kept: A fit_note (for their type): Framed as a conversation to understand process, not as a formal right to present evidence.
units.anchor: Invite the student to describe their process in detail
units.fit_note: Also gives the student a chance to respond.

units.why: 'Treat this as a teachable moment' for a first-time or unclear-policy case is the educative response, P68.
units.anchor: Treat this as a teachable moment

units.why: 'offer to let the student revise or resubmit the work with proper guidance' is a remedial response to unintended use (P68); not P38, which is a student-initiated window.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance differs (A neutral, B permit). Offering to let the student 'revise or resubmit the work' is a remedy for misuse, not a position on AI use, so neutral.
units.anchor: offer to let the student revise or resubmit the work with proper guidance

units.why: 'Document the Interaction' asks instructors to note what prompted concern and the outcome; this is a recordkeeping step in the procedure (P81), though not a report to a central office.
units.anchor: Document the Interaction
units.fit_note: Records are for the instructor's own use and to protect both sides, not a filing. Internal record-keeping, not filing a report with a central office.

units.why: 'Unintentional use + policy unclear = Education + no penalty or resubmission option' states the response in advance, so P37 (concrete consequences).
units.anchor: Unintentional use + policy unclear = Education + no penalty or resubmission option
units.fit_note: Suggested action, no penalty in this case.

units.why: 'Unintentional use + policy clear = Warning + resubmission or partial credit' states a graduated consequence (P37).
units.anchor: Unintentional use + policy clear = Warning + resubmission or partial credit

documents.title: AI Resources for Faculty
documents.summary: Provost page for faculty on generative AI. It encourages faculty to engage with AI, says what a syllabus statement should cover, and cites the Student Code of Conduct plagiarism definition that now includes AI-derived content. It states UM has no plagiarism detection software and that sanctions are for clear violations.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Your approach can range from restricting AI use to integrating it as a tool for learning', so it sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors. It adds only a conduct-code definition of plagiarism.

units.why: Says resources will be updated regularly while the university studies the effect on learning: P54, with a P55 flavor; chose P54 because no data is cited.
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A admin, B all). The page says the resources 'will be updated regularly'; it addresses all readers, so all.
units.anchor: will be updated regularly as we work to better understand the impact
units.fit_note: Also says the aim is to understand AI's impact on student learning. Also says the university is trying to understand AI's effect on student learning.

units.why: 'Faculty are encouraged to engage with these tools' encourages instructors to learn AI before setting policy (P63).
units.resolution_why: Type, phase and actor-relevant reading differ (A P63 before-course; B P59 general). 'Faculty are encouraged to engage with these tools' urges instructors to try AI and learn about it before deciding course practice, which P63 covers; P59 is for specific teaching tasks (B's fit_note: 'Encourages engagement in general, not a specific teaching task'). Specific tasks appear in the efficiency-tool unit. Other coder notes kept: B fit_note (for their type): Encourages engagement in general, not a specific teaching task.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to engage with these tools

units.why: 'Keep in mind the principles outlined in University Policy 370' ties AI use to existing university policy (P77).
units.anchor: Keep in mind the principles outlined in
units.fit_note: Policy 370 principles: stay informed, improve teaching, apply standards equitably.

units.why: 'Regularly update your course materials to reflect new developments ... including appropriate use of generative AI tools' asks for course redesign (P35).
units.resolution_why: Type differs (A P35, B P102). 'Regularly update your course materials to reflect new developments in your discipline, including appropriate use of generative AI tools' directs a change to course materials, not only staying informed (B's own fit_note), so P35 with a fit note. B's note: 'Is about updating course materials as AI changes, not only staying informed.' Other coder notes kept: B fit_note (for their type): Is about updating course materials as AI changes, not only staying informed.
units.anchor: Regularly update your course materials to reflect new developments in your discipline
units.fit_note: Asks for regular updating of course materials, including appropriate AI use, without naming an assignment or grading redesign.

units.why: 'incorporate AI ways that enhance student learning and career preparation' recommends teaching methods that include AI; tied to careers but is a course-change request (P35 over P44).
units.resolution_why: Type and phase differ (A P35 over-time; B P44 before-course). 'Continuously evaluate and refine your teaching methods to incorporate AI' asks instructors to keep revising their teaching, which is course redesign (P35) and ongoing (over-time). Career preparation is a stated aim (A's fit_note) but the instruction is about teaching methods. B's fit_note: 'Directs faculty to change their teaching, not students to learn AI.' Other coder notes kept: B fit_note (for their type): Directs faculty to change their teaching, not students to learn AI.
units.anchor: Continuously evaluate and refine your teaching methods
units.fit_note: Also gives career preparation as a reason.

units.why: 'Explore how you can use AI as an efficiency tool' is advice on instructor use of AI in teaching work (P59).
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B general). 'Explore how you can use AI as an efficiency tool' is advice to instructors on setting up their own work, so before-course.
units.anchor: Explore how you can use AI as an efficiency tool

units.why: 'Ensure that any integration of AI in your courses is done equitably, ensuring access for all students' is an equal-access duty (P51).
units.anchor: Ensure that any integration of AI in your courses is done equitably

units.why: Tells instructors to set clear expectations in syllabi: P09.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B course-start). Setting clear expectations for AI in the syllabus is communicating expectations, so course-start, as for other P09 units.
units.anchor: set clear expectations for the use of generative AI in your courses

units.why: 'Your approach can range from restricting AI use to integrating it as a tool for learning' leaves the choice to the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Your approach can range from restricting AI use to integrating it as a tool

units.why: 'Banning the use of generative AI is difficult to enforce' admits limits on control (P82).
units.anchor: Banning the use of generative AI is difficult to enforce

units.why: A good syllabus statement should define the scope of acceptable tools: P61.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B course-start). The item is what the syllabus statement should contain, so course-start.
units.anchor: A clear definition and scope of acceptable tools and their use
units.fit_note: Asks the syllabus to define scope, not a definition itself.

units.why: A syllabus statement should tie AI use to learning outcomes: P83.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B course-start). Same: a checklist item for the syllabus statement.
units.anchor: how they relate to the courses learning outcomes

units.why: The syllabus statement should cover integrity and attribution: P24 as the nearest.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B course-start). Same: a checklist item for the syllabus statement.
units.anchor: Academic integrity and attribution requirements
units.fit_note: Says what the statement should cover; it does not itself require students to cite. An item on a checklist for what the syllabus statement covers.

units.why: The syllabus statement should cover privacy and data security: P50.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B course-start). Same: a checklist item for the syllabus statement.
units.anchor: Privacy, Data Security, and Responsible Use
units.fit_note: Checklist item, no content on how to protect data.

units.why: Instructors must set citation standards using MLA, Chicago or APA: P24.
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A before-course, B course-start). 'Make sure to set standards for proper attribution and citation' is part of the syllabus expectations given to students, so course-start.
units.anchor: set standards for proper attribution and citation
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors, who set the attribution standard.

units.why: 'Student Code of Conduct now includes Generative AI in the definition of plagiarism' classifies AI misuse as plagiarism (P36).
units.resolution_why: Phase differs (A general, B when-misuse). 'now includes Generative AI in the definition of plagiarism' defines a term in the conduct code, so general (definitions).
units.anchor: now includes Generative AI in the definition of plagiarism

units.why: Quoted code definition forbids presenting AI-derived content as one's own: P19.
units.resolution_why: Phase and unit_stance differ (A general prohibit; B during-work restrict). The definition makes presenting AI-derived content 'as if it were the student's own original work' plagiarism. That binds the work students submit, so during-work, and it bans only passing AI content off as one's own (A's fit_note: not a ban on all AI use), so restrict.
units.anchor: content derived directly from a generative artificial intelligence tool
units.fit_note: A conduct code definition of plagiarism, not a ban on all AI use.

units.why: 'UM does not subscribe to any plagiarism detection software' says the university does not use detection software (P39).
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A admin, B all). 'UM does not subscribe to any plagiarism detection software' is a fact about the university's tools; admin.
units.anchor: UM does not subscribe to any plagiarism detection software
units.fit_note: Statement of fact about the university's tools. States absence of software, rather than unreliability.

units.why: Says there are "few reliable tools" that can prove AI plagiarism, a reason not to rely on detectors: P39, informs.
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A admin, B all). 'few reliable tools to detect generative AI' is a general fact about detectors for all readers; all.
units.anchor: few reliable tools to detect generative AI

units.why: Notes detector bias against international students: P39 (as part of the reason not to rely on detectors); P53 covers bias but of AI, not detectors.
units.resolution_why: Type and actor differ (A P53 admin; B P39 all). The sentence lists detector shortcomings ('limited capabilities, undesirable false positives rates', bias toward international students'), so it supports P39 (detectors unreliable); the bias is an instance of that unreliability, as in the matching detector unit on the teaching-center page. Actor all. Topics keep ethics-bias-environment.
units.anchor: bias towards the writing of international students

units.why: 'teach students that their human capacity for thought, imagination, and feeling far exceeds the ability of generative AI' is a recommended teaching message; no type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: Type, phase differ (A UNCOVERED course-start; B P32 before-course). 'The best approach is to teach students that their human capacity for thought, imagination, and feeling far exceeds the ability of generative AI' is a message instructors are told to teach, not a rule that students remain the primary problem-solver (B's fit_note: 'A message for instructors to teach, not a rule for students'). Constant comparison with P32 fails, so UNCOVERED with A's note; B's fit_note is kept as a note. Other coder notes kept: B fit_note (for their type): A message for instructors to teach, not a rule for students.
units.anchor: their human capacity for thought, imagination, and feeling far exceeds the ability of generative AI
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should teach students that human capacities exceed what generative AI can do.

units.why: 'Students need to learn the utility and limitations of Generative AI through preemptive instruction and corrective assessment' says students should be taught about AI, P70 (AI literacy), though it is addressed to instructors.
units.resolution_why: Type, phase differ (A P70 during-work; B P44 before-course). 'Students need to learn the utility and limitations of Generative AI through preemptive instruction and corrective assessment' calls for curricular AI literacy for students, which P70 covers; the career argument is the next sentence, coded P44. The instruction happens in the course, so during-work. B's fit_note: 'Includes limitations, and prescribes instruction and corrective assessment.' Other coder notes kept: B fit_note (for their type): Includes limitations, and prescribes instruction and corrective assessment.
units.anchor: Students need to learn the utility and limitations of Generative AI
units.fit_note: Delivered through instruction and corrective assessment in courses, not a training programme.

units.why: Career reason for teaching AI: P44.
units.resolution_why: Actor differs (A instructor, B all). 'vital preparation for their future careers where AI will likely be ubiquitous' is a rationale for all readers; all.
units.anchor: vital preparation for their future careers where AI will likely be ubiquitous

units.why: 'Misconduct investigations and official sanctions should be reserved for clear violations' sets a threshold for formal action (P69).
units.anchor: Misconduct investigations and official sanctions should be reserved for clear violations
units.fit_note: A threshold for escalating, which also favors educative responses. A threshold on when to investigate, not about the kind of evidence.

units.why: Discloses that ChatGPT 4 helped adapt the page, a process statement: P84.
units.resolution_why: Type and actor differ (A P48 admin; B P84 all). 'ChatGPT 4 was used to adapt the content on this website' tells how the guidance page was produced, not course materials (both coders' fit_notes). Same as the matching unit on the teaching-center page: P84, actor all. Other coder notes kept: A fit_note (for their type): Disclosure of AI use in creating the page, not course materials.
units.anchor: ChatGPT 4 was used to adapt the content on this website
units.fit_note: Also discloses AI use in producing the page.
